evals.prompt: Write a Rust kernel module for a platform device that registers with the device tree compatible string "vendor,my-device". On probe, it should allocate a KVec, store a greeting string, and schedule a delayed work item that prints the greeting after 5 jiffies. The module should clean up properly on unload. Use GPL license.
evals.expected_output: A complete, compilable Rust kernel module with module! macro, platform::Driver impl, pin-init initialization, workqueue usage, and proper error handling.
expectations: Uses module! macro with correct fields
Implements platform::Driver with probe returning PinInit
Uses #[pin_data] and #[pin] for the work field
Uses new_work! macro for work initialization
Implements WorkItem with run() method that prints via pr_info!
Uses impl_has_work! macro
Uses workqueue::system() or workqueue::system_long() to enqueue
Properly handles errors with ? and returns Result
Includes OF device ID table with compatible string
Uses GFP_KERNEL for allocations

evals.prompt: I need a PCI driver in Rust for a device with vendor ID 0x10EC and device ID 0x8168 (a Realtek network card). On probe, it should enable the PCI device, map BAR0 (region 0, size 256 bytes), read the first 4 bytes of the BAR (the vendor/device ID register), and log the value. It should also allocate a single MSI IRQ vector and register a dummy handler. Use proper error handling throughout.
evals.expected_output: A complete Rust kernel module implementing a PCI driver with BAR mapping, register read, MSI IRQ allocation, and device ID table.
expectations: Uses module_pci_driver! macro
Implements pci::Driver trait
Accesses PCI BAR via Bar type
Uses io memory to read from BAR offset
Allocates IRQ vectors with MSI flag
Registers an IRQ handler
Includes PCI device ID table
Proper error propagation with ?
Uses dev_info! for logging
Includes SPDX license header

evals.expected_output: A corrected version of the module explaining each fix. The Mutex needs pin-init, the GFP_KERNEL result needs to be handled, and the module struct needs #[pin_data] and #[pin] on the lock field.
expectations: Identifies that Mutex requires pin-init (cannot be directly constructed)
Correctly uses #[pin_data] attribute on struct
Correctly marks lock field with #[pin]
Uses InPlaceModule instead of Module (or uses try_pin_init!)
Handles the Result from v.push(..., GFP_KERNEL)?
Uses new_mutex! macro for initialization
Provides valid pin_init!/try_pin_init! expression
Explains why each change is needed
Uses proper pinned drop if needed (PinnedDrop)
Keeps original module! macro metadata intact
